title: A 36-Foot Fish May Be the Real Sea Serpent

scenes.text: A 36-foot fish may be the real sea serpent.
It's the giant oarfish, the longest bony fish alive.
It can reach thirty-six feet and six hundred pounds.
It swims by rippling a fin along its straight body.
It can live nearly 3,000 feet down.
Storms sometimes wash dying ones onto beaches.
Its ribbon body may have inspired sea serpent legends.

description:
A 36-foot fish may be the real sea serpent.
The giant oarfish is the longest bony fish alive, growing to about 36 feet and 600 pounds, and its ribbon-like body may have inspired sea serpent stories.
Would you swim next to one?
first_comment: Bonus: it typically lives around 650 feet down. Do you believe in sea monsters?
